messages:
maria: Hotfix request — async queue in eu-west2 is dropping ~0.8% of production inference requests since 22:50 UTC. Repro'd in staging with burst test. Small code change (backpressure tweak) ready: image rwd-inference:1.14.2-hotfix-queue. Change window is open 23:00-23:30 UTC. Requesting expedited canary + pin for full rollout. Runbook: https://runbook.redwood/hotfix-queue-8791

aj: Ack. Can we start with a 2-host canary instead of single? SRE signoff needed. Any perf regressions observed in staging?

priya: Staging run shows OK — CPU +2% at peak, latency p95 unchanged. No model changes. I can sign off SRE for canary.

drew: ops-oncall here — will monitor logs and add extra health checks for canary (/healthz, error_rate). Rollback plan: immediate rollback to rwd-inference:1.14.2 if error rate >0.5% sustained for 5m.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: job rwd-deploy-8791 -> canary eu-west2 hosts(2) using image rwd-inference:1.14.2-hotfix-queue. CI: green. Details: https://deploys.redwood/8791

jamie: I'll prep a short release note blurb: "Fix: reduce async queue drops under burst in eu-west" and add to release notes after deploy.

ops-oncall: Watching logs — so far no errors on canary hosts, traffic diverted successfully. Latency stable.

deploy-bot: Canary health update: 2/2 hosts green. Metrics snapshot: error_rate 0.12%, p95 latency unchanged. Promoting to 25% traffic now.

maria: Plan: promote to 25% then to 75% after 10m stable, then 100%. Confirming approvals: priya (SRE) + aj (release) + jamie (comms).

priya: :thumbsup: SRE approves full rollout if metrics remain within thresholds.

drew: If we see any spike during rollout, we rollback immediately and file an incident. Rollback helper: `./scripts/rollback.sh rwd-inference:1.14.2` (ops-oncall has creds).

deploy-bot: Rolling out to 75% -> in progress. ETA ~6m.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: 100% traffic on rwd-inference:1.14.2-hotfix-queue. Post-deploy checks passed. Dashboard: https://metrics.redwood/hotfix-8791

maria: Closing thread — hotfix deployed to prod. Root cause likely missing backpressure when consumer slower under short bursts. Follow-up action item created: INFR-452 (longer-term resilient queue redesign). Thanks all :rocket:

aj: Nice work team. I'll update CHANGELOG and mark this as hotfix in the release tracker."
